discoursePlan.expectedTakeaway: 在目前可取得的摘要或受限全文證據內，就「青少年短影音使用與睡眠、注意力及學業表現之關聯：跨研究設計的證據綜合與可能機制分析」而言，跨證據綜合支持一項受限回答：暴露、介入與結果之間的關聯證據的跨來源結果方向不完全一致，須依研究場域、方法與量測指標分別解讀。結論仍須分別考量研究場域、指標與方法差異。
discoursePlan.transitionToNext: 正文結束，後接實際引用的參考文獻。
limitations: 結論只能回收 ArgumentMap 中已有的主張與引用，不得把相關性改寫為因果，也不得超出摘要或全文實際揭露範圍。 本版不得外推至未取得全文的方法細節。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: Only frequency of posting on Facebook, but not general usage, was associated with poorer sleep quality.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 只有 Facebook 的發文頻率，而非一般使用情形，與較差的睡眠品質有關。
normalizedEvidence.topicCluster: relationship:一般社群媒體使用:睡眠品質

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: Results showed that, compared to those without SMD, users with SMD experienced elevated levels of loneliness and had less sleep on average, and during the weekdays in particular.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 與沒有社群媒體障礙者相比，具有社群媒體障礙的使用者孤獨感較高，平均睡眠時間較少，尤其是在平日。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: These preliminary findings showed that social media disorder across platforms and usage could potentially have different associations to mental health and sleep.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 初步研究結果顯示，不同平台上的社群媒體障礙與使用方式，可能與心理健康和睡眠呈現不同的關聯。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: Exploratory SEM analyses further indicate patterns consistent with indirect pathways: moderate watching is correlated with higher physical activity, which in turn is linked to lower depression; meanwhile, daily watching is correlated with later sleep timing, which is associated with higher depressive symptoms.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 探索性SEM顯示,每日觀看短影音與較晚睡眠時間相關,而較晚睡眠時間又與較高憂鬱症狀相關。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: These indirect effect analyses are constrained by the two-wave design and reliance on frequency-based measures, and should be interpreted as identifying plausible associations rather than establishing causal mediation.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 兩波設計與僅以頻率量測短影音使用限制了間接效果分析,因此結果只能辨識可能關聯,不能建立因果中介。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: Smoking did not show a significant mediating role.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 吸菸未呈現顯著中介作用。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: Using two waves of nationally representative data from the China Family Panel Studies, this study applies complementary analytical approaches: two-way fixed effects models (FE) to assess within-person associations, and cross-lagged structural equation modeling (SEM) to exploratorily examine temporal ordering and indirect pathways.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 研究使用中國家庭追蹤調查兩波全國代表性資料,以雙向固定效果模型估計個人內關聯,並以交叉滯後SEM探索時間順序與間接路徑。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: FE estimates suggest that moderate engagement with short videos is linked to lower subsequent levels of depressive symptoms, whereas habitual daily use shows no direct within-person association.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 固定效果估計顯示,適度觀看短影音與後續較低憂鬱症狀相關,但習慣性每日觀看沒有直接個人內關聯。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: Between-person results showed that for each hour adolescents used screens to communicate with friends across the day, sleep onset was later (11 ± 3 minutes, p < .01), sleep midpoint was later (8 ± 3 minutes, p < .01), and sleep duration was shorter (-5 ± 2 minutes, p < .03).
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 個人間分析顯示,每多一小時以螢幕與朋友溝通,入睡延後11 ± 3分鐘、睡眠中點延後8 ± 3分鐘、睡眠時長變化為−5 ± 2分鐘。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: Compared to the initial or substudy samples, participants from marginalized groups were less likely to be included in the final analyzed sample, including adolescents who were not White, adolescents whose mothers did not complete high school, adolescents whose family’s household income-to-poverty ratio was lower, and adolescents with single parents.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 最終分析樣本較少納入非白人、母親未完成高中、低所得及單親家庭青少年,構成選擇偏誤與一般化限制。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: Within-person results showed that on days when adolescents played video games more than their daytime average ± SE (1.3 ± 1.2 hours), sleep onset (6 ± 2 minutes, p < .01) and midpoint (4 ± 2 minutes, p < .02) were delayed for each additional hour of gaming.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 在個人內分析中,每多一小時超過本人平均的電玩時間,當晚入睡延後6 ± 2分鐘、睡眠中點延後4 ± 2分鐘。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: Of these adolescents, 475 provided three or more days/nights of valid daily survey and that night’s sleep data. The MIXED procedure (SAS 9.4) was used to examine the within- and between-person associations between daytime and evening screen-based activities and subsequent sleep timing and duration.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 475名青少年提供至少三日有效每日問卷與當夜睡眠資料,研究使用SAS MIXED程序進行個人內與個人間微縱向分析。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: Among adolescents, passive screen usage such as browsing the Internet or watching videos may not affect sleep timing or duration, but limiting interactive screen-based activities could protect adolescent sleep health and well-being.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 被動螢幕使用,例如瀏覽網路或觀看影片,可能不影響青少年的睡眠時間點或時長,與互動式活動結果形成對照。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: Adolescents who used screens to communicate with friends or play video games in the hour before bed had later sleep onset (30 ± 14 minutes, p < .03) and midpoint (25 ± 13 minutes, p < .05).
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 睡前一小時以螢幕與朋友溝通或玩電玩者,入睡延後30 ± 14分鐘且睡眠中點延後25 ± 13分鐘。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: We analyzed prospective cohort data from 9,398 early adolescents aged 11–12 years (48.4% female, 45% racial/ethnic minority) in the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development Study (Years 2–3, 2018–2021).
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 美國ABCD前瞻世代納入9,398名11至12歲早期青少年,使用第2至第3年資料檢驗一年後的睡眠結果。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: Having a television or Internet-connected electronic device in the bedroom was prospectively associated with shorter sleep duration one year later.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 臥室內有電視或連網電子裝置,前瞻性地與一年後較短睡眠時長相關。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: Regression analyses examined the associations between self-reported bedtime screen use (Year 2) and sleep variables (Year 3; self-reported sleep duration; caregiver-reported sleep disturbance), adjusting for sociodemographic covariates and sleep variables (Year 2).
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 迴歸模型以第2年睡前螢幕使用預測第3年睡眠,並調整社會人口共變項與第2年基線睡眠變項。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: Adolescents who left their phone ringer activated overnight had greater odds of experiencing sleep disturbance and experienced shorter sleep duration one year later, compared to those who turned off their phones at bedtime.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 相較睡前關閉手機鈴聲者,整夜開啟鈴聲的青少年一年後睡眠干擾勝算較高且睡眠時間較短。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: Talking/texting on the phone, listening to music, and using social media were all prospectively associated with shorter sleep duration, greater overall sleep disturbance, and a higher factor score for disorders of initiating and maintaining sleep one year later.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 睡前使用社群媒體、通話/傳訊及聽音樂均前瞻性地與一年後較短睡眠、較多整體睡眠干擾及較高入睡與睡眠維持障礙分數相關。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: Moreover, daytime screen exposure, including T.V. watching and social media use, and nighttime music listening were negatively associated with sleep quality. Conversely, nighttime screen time of shopping and working/studying positively influenced sleep quality.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 不同螢幕活動呈現混合方向:日間社群媒體與較差睡眠品質相關,但夜間購物及工作/學習螢幕時間與較佳睡眠品質相關。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: 831 participants underwent online assessment three times with interval of three months regarding their screen time and activities at specific times of the day, daytime sleepiness was assessed with the Epworth Sleepiness Scale, and sleep outcomes were assessed with the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index and Insomnia Severity Index.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 831名青少年以三個月間隔接受三波評估,並以Epworth嗜睡量表、PSQI及失眠嚴重度指數測量睡眠結果。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: Whereas no cross-lag and predictive effects of sleep outcomes on screen time were revealed.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 模型未發現睡眠結果對後續螢幕時間的交叉滯後或預測效果。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: The RI_CLPM model revealed that both electronic screen time during daytime and after lights off in the evening in Wave1 negatively predicted the sleep quality in Wave2; the nighttime screen time before lights off in Wave1 significantly negatively predicted the severity of insomnia in Wave2.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 第一波的日間螢幕時間與熄燈後螢幕時間均負向預測第二波睡眠品質,熄燈前夜間螢幕時間則負向預測第二波失眠嚴重度。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: The associations between time spent on various screen activities, and sleep outcomes were examined respectively after controlling for inter-individual differences using the Random Intercept Cross-Lagged Panel Model models and LMMs.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 研究使用隨機截距交叉滯後模型與線性混合模型,控制個體間差異後檢驗螢幕活動與睡眠的關聯。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: We conducted a systematic review of studies including young people aged 16-25 years. We searched Medline, Web of Science, and CINAHL for observational studies, identifying 60 studies. These studies were assessed for methodological quality. Only studies rated as moderate or high-quality studies were included (n = 42).
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 該系統性回顧納入了年齡16至25歲青少年的觀察性研究，並從辨識出的60項研究中保留了42項被評為中度或高度品質的研究。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: In summary, digital media use was associated to shorter sleep duration and poorer sleep quality.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 數位媒體使用與較短的睡眠時長及較差的睡眠品質有關。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: Additional research is warranted to draw solid conclusions about the causal direction and to understand the underlying mechanisms.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 仍需要進一步研究，才能對因果方向作出確切結論並了解其 underlying mechanisms。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: The results revealed that attentional impulsivity was positively associated with SVU. Both attentional impulsivity and SVU were positively related to school misbehavior, controlling for covariates.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 注意力衝動性與 SVU 呈正相關；在控制共變項後，注意力衝動性與 SVU 都與學校不當行為呈正相關。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: Moreover, active parental media mediation strategies were found to mediate the relationship between attentional impulsivity and school misbehavior.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 研究發現，積極的家長媒體調 medi策略在注意力衝動性與學校不當行為之間的關係中具有中介作用。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: A self-reported questionnaire survey with parental informed consent was collected from 2021 to 2022. A purposive sampling method was employed. Two middle schools and two high schools were selected in two provinces (i.e., Liaoning and Sichuan) in mainland China. The selected provinces represent the national average in terms of educational development level (Y. Guo & Li, 2024 ) and offer a balanced economic profile with 2021 GDPs that fall both below and above the national mean (Zhou, 2022 ). The selection of two middle schools and two high schools within these provinces was conducted in a convenient manner.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 研究於2021至2022年以家長知情同意的自陳問卷蒐集資料,採目的抽樣,並便利選取中國遼寧與四川兩省的兩所國中及兩所高中。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: Following Bányai ( 2017 ) and Hussain and Wegmann ( 2021 ), SVU was measured by the total amount of daily SVU time.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 短影音使用以過去6個月平日與週末/假日的平均每日使用小時分別量測,使用時數越高代表使用越多。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: A total of 1006 students were invited to participate, and 839 valid responses were collected, yielding a response rate of 83.4%. Regarding the samples, more than half of them were male (i.e., 55.90%) and around 15–16 years old ( M = 15.62, SD = 1.18).
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 研究邀請1006名學生,取得839份有效回覆,回覆率83.4%;樣本55.90%為男性,平均年齡15.62歲(SD = 1.18)。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: An instrument of school misbehavior consisting of 17 items was modified from Daddis & Meadows ( 2021 ) using the translation and back-translation method. An expert panel consisting of three faculty members in social work and criminology consensually selected this scale, as its items were appropriate for the Chinese context.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 學校不當行為工具由17題構成,經翻譯與回譯並由三名社會工作與犯罪學教師組成的專家小組選定。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: Using a cross-sectional design, a sample of Chinese adolescents (N = 839) was employed.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 研究採橫斷面設計,納入839名中國青少年,並以結構方程模型檢驗所提出的關係。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: Drawing on the parental mediation theory, the current study examined the associations of SVU and attentional impulsivity with adolescents’ school misbehaviors, as well as the mediating role of parental mediation.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 研究以家長媒體中介理論檢驗短影音使用、注意力衝動性與青少年學校不當行為的關聯,以及家長中介的中介角色。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: Potential interventions are recommended to focus on active parental media mediation strategies, such as engaging in open discussions with children. Interventions targeting adolescents’ self-esteem or related factors should also be considered.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 作者建議介入聚焦積極的家長媒體中介,例如與兒童進行開放討論,並考慮青少年的自尊或相關因素。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: Patterns of significant associations for late sleep onset and wake times remained unchanged, although effect sizes were reduced, particularly for very high social media use.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 較晚入睡與醒來的關聯在全面調整後仍存在,但效果幅度降低,尤其在極高度使用者中。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: The most recent survey (sweep 6 at around age 14) gathered self-report data from 11 872 cohort members, including questions on their typical social media use and sleep patterns.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 英國千禧世代研究第6波約14歲時取得11 872名成員的社群媒體使用與睡眠型態自陳資料。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: Separate binomial logistic regression models predicted ORs of each sleep outcome for low, high and very high social media users, compared with average users. We ran models that controlled only for exact age and sex, followed by models that further controlled for measures of demographics, family characteristics, psychological well-being and health.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 研究先控制精確年齡與性別,再進一步控制人口、家庭特徵、心理福祉與健康,以二元邏輯斯迴歸比較不同社群媒體使用層級。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: Very high social media was no longer significantly associated with long sleep onset latency; however, its association with frequent nighttime awakenings remained significant but smaller.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 全面調整後,極高度社群媒體使用與長入睡潛伏期不再顯著;其與頻繁夜醒的關聯仍顯著但幅度較小。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: High social media use was no longer significantly associated with long sleep onset latency or frequent nighttime awakenings.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 全面調整後,高度社群媒體使用不再與長入睡潛伏期或頻繁夜間醒來顯著相關。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: During the experimental phase, compared to baseline condition, progressively limiting short video exposure to 30 and 0 min increased sleep efficiency by 5.43% and 11.51%, respectively, reduced Wakefulness After Sleep Onset by 35.3 min and 46.4 min, raised positive effect scores by 2.33 and 5.44 points, and improved N-back accuracy by 3.5% and 5.5%.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 相較基線,將短影音限制至30與0分鐘時,睡眠效率分別提高5.43%與11.51%,入睡後清醒時間分別減少35.3與46.4分鐘。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: To explore aforementioned factors quantitatively, 18 University students were recruited as participants. They were sequentially exposed to three conditions: a 60 min baseline, a 30 min condition and a 0 min condition.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 受控交叉研究招募18名大學生,依序接受60分鐘基線、30分鐘及0分鐘三種睡前短影音條件。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: Polysomnography technology was used to continuously monitor electroencephalogram, electro-ophthalmogram and other signals during sleep. Subsequently, participants were asked to complete a subjective-response questionnaire and an early-morning cognitive assessment.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 研究以多導睡眠監測腦電、眼電等睡眠訊號,並在翌晨進行主觀問卷與認知評估。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: Baseline survey data (N = 211) revealed that 89.6% of university students used smartphones pre-bedtime and 64.5% watched short-form videos.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 211人的基線調查中,89.6%睡前使用智慧型手機,64.5%觀看短影音。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: Using an online survey of college students ( N = 549) from two U.S. universities, structural equation modeling revealed
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 研究使用來自美國兩所大學、549名大學生的線上問卷，並採用結構方程模型進行分析。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: individuals with lower self-control, stronger habitual SFV use, and greater involvement (enjoyment, escapism, and social connectedness) were more prone to procrastinatory SFV use
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 自我控制力較低、短影音使用習慣較強，以及投入程度較高（享受、逃避與社會連結）的人，更容易拖延性地使用短影音。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: procrastinatory SFV use, which in turn was associated with higher stress levels, poorer overall sleep quality, longer sleep latency, more sleep disturbances, and greater daytime dysfunction, but not with academic performance
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 拖延性短影音使用與較高的壓力程度、較差的整體睡眠品質、較長的入睡潛伏期、較多的睡眠干擾及較嚴重的日間功能障礙有關，但與學業表現無關。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: To address this gap, this study investigated the motivational factors underlying procrastinatory SFV use and its relationship with user well-being.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 研究旨在探討拖延性短影音使用的動機因素及其與使用者福祉的關係。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: Theoretical contributions to the study of irrational media use, practical recommendations for mitigating procrastinatory SFV engagement, and directions for longitudinal and context-sensitive future research are discussed.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 作者提出未來應進行縱貫且具情境敏感性的研究。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: Synthesis was done by summarizing results across studies by age groups of 0–5, 6–12, and 13–15 years within four sleep domains: Bedtime and sleep onset; Sleep quality; Sleep duration; Daytime tiredness.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 該回顧按0–5歲、6–12歲及13–15歲年齡組，針對四個睡眠領域整合研究結果：就寢與入睡、睡眠品質、睡眠時長及日間疲倦。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: Methodological quality was rated using the Quality Assessment Tool for Quantitative Studies by two independent reviewers.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 兩名獨立評閱者使用《量化研究品質評估工具》評估研究方法品質。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: Inclusion criteria included age ≤ 15 years, and intervention, cohort, or cross-sectional studies from western countries.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 該系統性回顧納入來自西方國家、研究對象為15歲或以下兒童的介入、世代或橫斷研究。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: Searches were carried out in four databases (CINAHL, Web of Science, EMBASE, and Medline).
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 回顧搜尋CINAHL、Web of Science、EMBASE與Medline四個資料庫。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: The study designs were randomized controlled trials (n = 3), quasi-experimental studies (n = 2), prospective cohort studies (n = 15), and cross-sectional studies (n = 29).
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 納入研究包括3項隨機對照試驗、2項準實驗研究、15項前瞻性世代研究及29項橫斷面研究。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: The evidence for a relationship between electronic media use and other sleep outcomes was more inconclusive. However, for 6-12-year-old children, there was evidence for associations of electronic media use with delayed bedtime and poor sleep quality. For 13-15-year-olds, there was evidence for associations between screen time and problems falling asleep, and between social media use and poor sleep quality.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 電子媒體使用與睡眠時長以外睡眠結果之間的證據較不確定;6至12歲有延後就寢與睡眠品質不佳的關聯證據,13至15歲則有螢幕時間與入睡困難、社群媒體使用與睡眠品質不佳的關聯證據。
normalizedEvidence.topicCluster: relationship:一般社群媒體使用:睡眠品質

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: Studies with stronger research design and of higher quality are needed to draw solid conclusions about electronic media's impact on other sleep outcomes.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 作者指出需要更強研究設計與更高品質的研究,才能對電子媒體影響其他睡眠結果作出穩固結論。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: Evidence for an association between electronic media use and sleep duration was identified, with stronger evidence for 6-15-years-olds than 0-5-year-olds.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 電子媒體使用與睡眠時長關聯的證據,在6至15歲族群比0至5歲族群更強。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: Overall, electronic media use was generally associated with shorter sleep duration in children and adolescents.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 整體而言,電子媒體使用通常與兒童及青少年較短的睡眠時長相關。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: The search identified 10,719 unique studies, of which 109 fulfilled inclusion and exclusion criteria and were assessed for methodological quality. In total, 49 studies were included in the review.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 搜尋辨識10719篇不重複研究,其中109篇符合納排條件並接受方法品質評估,最終納入49篇。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: This systematic review examines the evidence of electronic media use related to sleep among 0-15-year-olds.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 系統性回顧檢視0至15歲兒童與青少年電子媒體使用和睡眠相關的證據。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: Social anxiety partially mediates the relationship between short-form video addiction and sleep quality.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 社交焦慮部分中介了短影音成癮與睡眠品質之間的關係。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: Short‐form video addiction, sleep quality, and social anxiety are significantly correlated ( r = 0.439, 0.404, 0.457, P < 0.001).
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 短影音成癮、睡眠品質與社交焦慮之間呈顯著相關（r = 0.439、0.404、0.457，P < 0.001）。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: A questionnaire survey was conducted in this cross-sectional study on 1629 adolescents recruited from three high schools.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 本橫斷面研究對招募自三所高中的1629名青少年進行了問卷調查。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: Schools are recommended to implement measures to promote sleep quality among adolescents.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 作者建議學校採取措施促進青少年的睡眠品質。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: The indirect effect exerted through social anxiety is 0.149, accounting for 37.6%.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 經社交焦慮產生的間接效果為0.149,占總效果37.6%。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: The direct effect of short-form video addiction on sleep quality is 0.248, accounting for 62.4% of the total effect.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 短影音成癮對睡眠品質的直接效果為0.248,占總效果62.4%。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: This study examined the effect of short-form video addiction on adolescents’ sleep quality, as well as the mediating role of social anxiety, to identify methods for improving adolescents’ sleep quality in the Internet era.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 研究旨在檢驗短影音成癮對青少年睡眠品質的影響,以及社交焦慮的中介角色。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: Participants’ sleep quality score is 6.12 ± 3.29 points.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 參與者的睡眠品質分數為6.12 ± 3.29分。
normalizedEvidence.topicCluster: relationship:短影音成癮:睡眠品質分數

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: The detection rate of sleep quality among them is 31.06%.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 參與者睡眠品質問題的檢出率為31.06%。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: Their short-form video addiction, social anxiety, and sleep quality were evaluated using corresponding scales.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 研究以相應量表評估短影音成癮、社交焦慮與睡眠品質,並使用Pearson相關分析及AMOS 20.0中介效果分析。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: Therefore, this study collected 1052 valid questionnaires from elementary school students, attempting to explore the possibility that their short video usage might negatively impact their academic performance.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 本研究收集了1052份小學生的有效問卷。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: The research findings indicate that the more elementary school students use short videos, the lower their academic performance, with attention mediating in this relationship.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 在受研究的小學生中，短影音使用越多與較低的學業表現相關。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: The research findings indicate that the more elementary school students use short videos, the lower their academic performance, with attention mediating in this relationship.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 注意力在短影音使用與學業表現之間發揮了中介作用。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: We found a high prevalence of DES (63.7%) and PSQ (51.2%).
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 研究發現數位眼疲勞的盛行率為63.7%，睡眠品質不佳的盛行率為51.2%。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: Extended daily digital media use (>4 hours), bedtime usage, older age, female sex, online education and DES were significantly associated with PSQ.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 每日延長使用數位媒體超過4小時、睡前使用、年齡較大、女性、線上教育以及數位眼疲勞，均與睡眠品質不佳顯著相關。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: A cross-sectional survey of 512 participants (aged 11–18 years) assessed DES and PSQ using the Computer Vision Syndrome Questionnaire and the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 橫斷面調查納入512名11至18歲參與者,使用電腦視覺症候群問卷與匹茲堡睡眠品質指數評估數位眼疲勞與睡眠品質不佳。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: Data analysis was conducted utilizing SPSS software (version 22.0). We presented descriptive statistics in the form of frequencies and percentages. To examine the relationships and differences within the data, we employed the Chi-Square Test and logistic regression analyses. To adjust for the risk of type I errors due to multiple comparisons, a Bonferroni correction was applied. Criteria for statistical significance were set at a p-value of less than 0.05 and results were reported alongside a 95% confidence interval (CI) to ensure precision in our findings.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 分析使用SPSS 22.0、卡方檢定與邏輯斯迴歸,套用Bonferroni校正,顯著水準為p < 0.05,並報告95%信賴區間。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: This study aims to investigate the prevalence of DES and sleep problems among adolescents, exploring their interconnectedness and identifying potential risk factors.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 研究旨在調查青少年數位眼疲勞與睡眠問題的盛行率、兩者關聯及潛在風險因子。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: The study included 512 individuals with complete data. Table 1 details participant demographics, including gender, age, and digital media usage patterns. The mean age of the participants was 14.5 ± 2.0 years, with 50.6% in early adolescence (11–14 years) and 49.4% in mid to late adolescence (15–18 years). Additionally, 58.2% of the participants were female.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 512名完整資料參與者的平均年齡為14.5 ± 2.0歲,58.2%為女性。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: A majority of the participants (51.6%) reported using digital media for over four hours daily. It was observed that older adolescents tend to use digital media for significantly longer periods (X 2 = 13.184, df = 2, p = 0.001, Fig 2 ).
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 51.6%的參與者回報每日使用數位媒體超過四小時,且年齡較大的青少年使用時間顯著較長(X2 = 13.184,df = 2,p = 0.001)。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: This cross-sectional study collected data via questionnaires administered to adolescents (aged 11–18 years) attending the ophthalmology outpatient clinic between November 22, 2021, and June 3, 2022, in Edirne, Turkey.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 問卷資料於2021年至2022年間在土耳其Edirne的眼科門診向11至18歲青少年蒐集。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: Despite 52% of participants expressing a preference for nighttime digital media usage, a notable 84.2% admitted to using digital media within the hour leading up to bedtime. Furthermore, it was discovered that older adolescents significantly favor the use of digital media during the night (X 2 = 27.349, df = 1, p<0.001) and just before sleeping (X 2 = 21.237, df = 1, p<0.001, Fig 3 ).
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 84.2%的參與者表示在睡前1小時內使用數位媒體;年齡較大的青少年更偏好夜間與睡前使用。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: Preferring a night-time digital media use was not significantly associated with the percentage of DES but was significantly associated with PSQ (p = 0.001). Digital media use before bedtime was associated with an increase in both DES and PSQ percentage (p<0.001, Table 1 ).
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 偏好夜間使用數位媒體與睡眠品質不佳顯著相關(p = 0.001),睡前使用則與數位眼疲勞及睡眠品質不佳比例增加相關(p < 0.001)。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: Findings suggest that while short-form videos can be valuable tools for learning and entertainment, excessive consumption may contribute to attention deficits and limited exposure to diverse viewpoints.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 短影音可以是有價值的學習與娛樂工具。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: Findings suggest that while short-form videos can be valuable tools for learning and entertainment, excessive consumption may contribute to attention deficits and limited exposure to diverse viewpoints.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 研究結果顯示，過度使用可能導致接觸多元觀點的機會受限。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: Findings suggest that while short-form videos can be valuable tools for learning and entertainment, excessive consumption may contribute to attention deficits and limited exposure to diverse viewpoints.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 研究結果顯示，過度使用可能導致注意力缺陷。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: Also, their SVA daily usage negatively correlates with working memory and verbal ability, which both simultaneously mediate between their user behavior and poorer academic performance.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 對年齡較小的組別而言，短影音應用程式的每日使用量與工作記憶及語文能力呈負相關，而這兩者同時中介使用者行為與較差學業表現之間的關係。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: The findings reveal that daily usage of SVA is negatively correlated with users’ ADOG and academic performance for both age cohorts.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 短影音應用程式的每日使用量與兩個年齡組使用者的學業延宕滿足及學業表現呈負相關。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: And the dependency on algorithmic personalization negatively predicts the working memory, verbal ability and academic performance of the younger cohort only.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 對演算法個人化的依賴僅在年齡較小的組別中負向預測工作記憶、語文能力及學業表現。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: A sample of Chinese adolescents from two age cohorts (Mage=12.25, SD=0.02, N=454; Mage=15.21, SD=0.02, N= 368) completed the survey on SVA user behavior and cognitive ability test regarding academic delay of gratification (ADOG), working memory and verbal ability.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 參與者完成短影音使用行為問卷,並接受學業延宕滿足、工作記憶與語文能力的認知能力測驗。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: This study aimed to examine whether and how adolescents’ user behaviors regarding SVA, including daily usage and reliance on algorithmic recommendations, predict their cognitive functioning and academic performance.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 研究旨在檢驗青少年的短影音應用程式每日使用量與演算法推薦依賴,是否以及如何預測認知功能與學業表現。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: A sample of Chinese adolescents from two age cohorts (Mage=12.25, SD=0.02, N=454; Mage=15.21, SD=0.02, N= 368) completed the survey on SVA user behavior and cognitive ability test regarding academic delay of gratification (ADOG), working memory and verbal ability.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 樣本包含兩個中國青少年年齡群:平均12.25歲、454人,以及平均15.21歲、368人。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: Considering the age differences in SVA-related effects, the study further points out the higher susceptibility of younger adolescents to SVA use compared to their older counterparts, which should be noted by students, parents, educators and researchers to prevent the potentially negative impact.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 作者指出年齡較小的青少年相較於年齡較大的青少年,對短影音使用相關影響的易感性較高。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: Research has shown that increased screen time, particularlybefore bedtime, disrupts sleep quality, amount of sleep and circadian rhythms.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 研究顯示，增加螢幕使用時間，尤其是在睡前，會干擾睡眠品質、睡眠時長與晝夜節律。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: Thedisruption of sleep, in turn, can influence attention, memory and learning, which is directlyassociated with academic performance.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 睡眠受干擾進而可能影響注意力、記憶與學習，而這些又直接與學業表現相關。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: Existingresearch has some limitations, such as mostly depending on surveys and self-report data, notusing experimental methods and not focusing on digital media content.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 現有研究存在一些限制，例如主要依賴問卷與自陳資料、未採用實驗方法，也未聚焦於數位媒體內容。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: The multi-component intervention significantly improved sleep quality in both groups, with PSQI scores decreasing by 3.6 points in the personalized algorithm group and 2.8 points in the community-based group (p < 0.001, Cohen’s d = 1.71 and 1.46, respectively).
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 多成分介入後,個人化與社群式演算法兩組PSQI分別下降3.6與2.8分(p < 0.001;Cohen’s d分別為1.71與1.46)。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: Entertainment content had the most detrimental effects on sleep parameters compared to knowledge and information content (p < 0.001, η2 = 0.23).
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 娛樂內容對睡眠參數的不利程度高於知識與資訊內容(p < 0.001,η2 = 0.23)。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: Our sample consisted exclusively of college students from a single university in China, limiting generalizability to other age groups, educational backgrounds, cultural contexts, or populations with different usage patterns.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 樣本僅來自中國單一大學,限制對其他年齡、教育與文化脈絡的外推,尤其不能直接外推至青少年。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: The eight-week duration, while sufficient to demonstrate immediate effects, does not provide information about long-term sustainability of improvements.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 八週研究只能顯示即時變化,不能判斷介入改善能否長期維持。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: Our study design did not include a no-intervention control group, which limits our ability to attribute all observed improvements specifically to the intervention rather than to natural fluctuations, regression to the mean, or placebo effects.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 研究未設無介入對照組,因此不能把全部前後改善歸因於介入,而排除自然波動、平均數回歸或安慰劑效果。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: Sixty college students (aged 18–25) meeting criteria for short video addiction (PSQI ≥5, daily usage ≥2 h) were randomly assigned to personalized algorithm (n = 30) or community-based algorithm (n = 30) groups.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 18至25歲、PSQI至少5分且每日短影音至少2小時的大學生,被隨機分至個人化演算法或社群式演算法組,各30人。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: Personalized algorithms significantly worsened sleep quality compared to community-based algorithms (PSQI: 10.4 ± 2.3 vs. 8.7 ± 2.1, p = 0.003, Cohen’s d = 0.77).
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 個人化演算法組睡眠品質較社群式演算法組差(PSQI 10.4 ± 2.3比8.7 ± 2.1;p = 0.003;Cohen’s d = 0.77)。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: Reduced short video usage time significantly mediated the relationship between the intervention and improved PSQI scores (indirect effect = −1.42, 95% CI: −1.89, −0.95, p < 0.001), accounting for 44.3% of the total effect.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 短影音使用時間降低中介介入與PSQI改善的關係(間接效果−1.42;95% CI −1.89至−0.95;p < 0.001),占總效果44.3%。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: Although total screen time did not significantly predict academic achievement, it showed a moderate negative correlation with sleep quality (r = −0.18, p < 0.01).
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 儘管總螢幕使用時間無法顯著預測學業成就，但其與睡眠品質呈中度負相關（r = −0.18，p < 0.01）。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: A descriptive correlational study was conducted among 477 students aged 12–14 years from four randomly selected schools in northern Jordan.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 一項描述性相關研究以約旦北部四所隨機選取學校的477名12至14歲學生為對象進行。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: Weekend screen time emerged as a significant negative predictor of sleep quality (β = −0.27, p = 0.016).
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 週末螢幕使用時間是睡眠品質的顯著負向預測因子（β = −0.27，p = 0.016）。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: This study aimed to examine screen time patterns among Jordanian adolescents and assess their associations with sleep quality and academic achievement.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 研究旨在描述約旦青少年的螢幕時間型態,並評估其與睡眠品質及學業成就的關聯。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: Gender and school type were also significant predictors.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 性別與學校類型亦是睡眠品質的顯著預測因子。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: Results showed that average screen time was 9.13 h per day.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 青少年的平均每日螢幕時間為9.13小時。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: Adolescents with screen devices in their bedrooms and those with chronic medical conditions reported higher screen time.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 臥室內有螢幕裝置及患有慢性疾病的青少年,回報較高的螢幕時間。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: Participants completed the validated Questionnaire for Screen Time of Adolescents (QueST) and the Adolescent Sleep–Wake Scale–Short Version (ASWS-S), while academic performance was assessed using GPA from school records.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 參與者完成經驗證的青少年螢幕時間問卷與青少年睡眠-清醒量表短版,學業表現則使用學校紀錄的GPA評估。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: Interventions targeting screen habits could help enhance sleep and potentially benefit academic performance.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 作者認為針對螢幕使用習慣的介入可能改善睡眠,並可能有益於學業表現。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: These findings indicated that strict parental rules seem to prevent subsequent sleep problems, i.e., low quality of sleep and delayed bedtime, particularly among adolescents who reported low levels of (problematic) social media use. Among adolescents who reported high levels of (problematic) social media use, strict parenting did not affect sleep quality or bedtime.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 嚴格睡前網路規則只在低程度社群媒體使用者中與較少後續睡眠問題一致;高度投入使用者的睡眠品質或就寢時間未受嚴格規則影響。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: When we tested the effects of the frequency of social media use and problematic social media use simultaneously, only the effect of the frequency of social media use on bedtime one year later was significant (β = 0.13, p < 0.01).
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 同時納入使用頻率與問題性使用後,只有社群媒體使用頻率仍顯著預測一年後較晚就寢(β = 0.13,p < 0.01)。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: Participants who dropped out were more likely to report more frequent social media use (t(2704) = 5.40, p < 0.001), more problematic social media use (t(2630) = −2.63, p = 0.008), later times of going to sleep (t(2500) = −9.69, p < 0.001), and poorer quality of sleep (t(2598) = 2.09, p = 0.04).
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 流失者在第一波回報較頻繁與較問題性的社群媒體使用、較晚就寢及較差睡眠品質,顯示差異性流失偏誤。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: The previously found effect of problematic use on later bedtimes was not significant (β = 0.04, n.s.).
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 同時納入兩種暴露後,問題性社群媒體使用對一年後較晚就寢的效果衰減為不顯著(β = 0.04)。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: The effect of problematic social media use on the perceived quality of sleep was non-significant.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 問題性社群媒體使用對自覺睡眠品質的縱向效果未達顯著。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: In these models, we also controlled for gender, age, educational level, and the outcome variables at T1.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 結構方程模型控制性別、年齡、教育層級及第一波結果變項。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: The present two-wave longitudinal study of 2021 secondary school students (Mage = 13.86, SD = 1.25) examined whether frequency of social media use and problematic social media use predicted adolescents’ bedtime and quality of sleep.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 兩波縱向研究納入2,021名中學生,平均年齡13.86歲,檢驗社群媒體使用頻率與問題性使用對睡眠時間及品質的預測。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: A questionnaire was sent to Thai and international high school students via a Google Forms link. The questionnaire contained 39 questions, asking participants about their demographic data and short-form video use rate, as well as the attention assessment.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 研究透過 Google Forms 連結向泰國及國際高中生發放問卷，詢問其人口統計資料、短影音使用頻率及注意力評估。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: Regarding usage, 35% continually watched multiple short-form videos for over 1 hour, and 70% uploaded their videos on the platform at least once. Instagram was the most frequently used among students.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 35% 的參與者會連續觀看多部短影音超過 1 小時，而 Instagram 是學生最常使用的平台。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: Short-term memory was measured using the ME Test, a subtest of the Intelligenz Struktur Test (IST), which assesses the ability to recall a series of words.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 短期記憶使用智力結構測驗（IST）的子測驗 ME Test 進行測量，該測驗評估回憶一系列詞語的能力。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: The participants were 40 students selected through random sampling.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 參與者為40名透過隨機抽樣選出的學生。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: An experimental method with a two-group design was employed, consisting of an experimental group that watched short duration videos for 180 seconds and a control group that received no video exposure prior to the memory test.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 研究採用雙組實驗設計，實驗組觀看短時長影片180秒，對照組在記憶測驗前未接受影片暴露。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: This study aimed to examine the effect of short duration video exposure on short-term memory performance among students at Yayasan Irtiqo Kebajikan.
normalizedEvidence.normalizedClaimZhTw: 研究旨在檢驗短時長影片暴露對Yayasan Irtiqo Kebajikan學生短期記憶表現的影響。

normalizedEvidence.originalSpan: The Influence of Short-Duration Video Content on Short-Term Memory in Junior High School Students (A Study of 30 Students at Yayasan Irtiqo Kebajikan)

acceptedSources.title: Adolescents’ short-form video addiction and sleep quality: the mediating role of social anxiety
acceptedSources.abstract: Abstract Background Adolescence is a critical period for individual growth and development. Insufficient sleep adversely affects adolescents’ physical development, blood pressure, vision, and cognitive function. This study examined the effect of short-form video addiction on adolescents’ sleep quality, as well as the mediating role of social anxiety, to identify methods for improving adolescents’ sleep quality in the Internet era. Methods A questionnaire survey was conducted in this cross-sectional study on 1629 adolescents recruited from three high schools. Their short-form video addiction, social anxiety, and sleep quality were evaluated using corresponding scales. Pearson correlation analysis was carried out to analyze the relationships among short‐form video addiction, sleep quality, and social anxiety. Mediating effect analysis was constructed using AMOS 20.0 statistical software. Results Participants’ sleep quality score is 6.12 ± 3.29 points. The detection rate of sleep quality among them is 31.06%. Short‐form video addiction, sleep quality, and social anxiety are significantly correlated ( r = 0.439, 0.404, 0.457, P < 0.001). The direct effect of short-form video addiction on sleep quality is 0.248, accounting for 62.4% of the total effect. The indirect effect exerted through social anxiety is 0.149, accounting for 37.6%. Conclusions Sleep disorders are very common among Chinese adolescents. Short‐form video addiction is positively correlated with adolescents’ sleep quality and social anxiety. Social anxiety partially mediates the relationship between short-form video addiction and sleep quality. The adverse effects of short-form video addiction and social anxiety on the sleep quality of this group must be minimized. Schools are recommended to implement measures to promote sleep quality among adolescents.

Short‐form video addiction, sleep quality, and social anxiety are significantly correlated ( r = 0.439, 0.404, 0.457, P < 0.001). A questionnaire survey was conducted in this cross-sectional study on 1629 adolescents recruited from three high schools. This study examined the effect of short-form video addiction on adolescents’ sleep quality, as well as the mediating role of social anxiety, to identify methods for improving adolescents’ sleep quality in the Internet era. Their short-form video addiction, social anxiety, and sleep quality were evaluated using corresponding scales. Pearson correlation analysis was carried out to analyze the relationships among short‐form video addiction, sleep quality, and social anxiety. Mediating effect analysis was constructed using AMOS 20.0 statistical software. Participants’ sleep quality score is 6.12 ± 3.29 points. The detection rate of sleep quality among them is 31.06%. The direct effect of short-form video addiction on sleep quality is 0.248, accounting for 62.4% of the total effect. The indirect effect exerted through social anxiety is 0.149, accounting for 37.6%. Schools are recommended to implement measures to promote sleep quality among adolescents.

acceptedSources.title: The relationship between short video usage and academic achievement among elementary school students: The mediating effect of attention and the moderating effect of parental short video usage
acceptedSources.abstract: Short videos have gained widespread popularity among elementary school students in China. As a form of entertainment media, their usage has steadily increased among adolescents in recent years. This phenomenon has sparked extensive discussions in society, especially against Chinese parents’ high concern for their children’s academic performance. Therefore, this study collected 1052 valid questionnaires from elementary school students, attempting to explore the possibility that their short video usage might negatively impact their academic performance. Besides, the mechanism of this relationship was also examined from the perspective of children’s attention and environmental factors of parents’ short video usage. The research findings indicate that the more elementary school students use short videos, the lower their academic performance, with attention mediating in this relationship. The longer the parental short video usage duration, the exacerbating effect it has on elementary school students’ negative impact on attention caused by short video usage due to its positive moderating effect. This study provides crucial insights for parents, educators, and short video platforms, offering valuable references for formulating more scientifically and logically grounded educational strategies.

extractedSections.heading: 1. Introduction
extractedSections.text: Short videos provide visual stimulation to the audience through techniques such as sound, light, and images [ 1 ]. This multimedia format is widely popular and has deeply integrated into various aspects of social life [ 2 ]. Short video applications like TikTok and Kwai have gained prominence in the wave of mobile internet and have become popular choices among young users globally [ 3 ]. Users of these applications typically watch and create short videos for entertainment and information while actively participating in social interactions [ 4 ]. The characteristics of short video apps, such as their brevity, mobility, entertainment value, vertical format, and interactivity, cater perfectly to the social needs of various audiences [ 5 ]. In China, the user base of short video apps has reached 962 hundreds of million, accounting for 91.5% of the overall Internet users [ 6 ]. Of particular concern is that minors, especially elementary school students, have become significant users of short video apps. The "Youth Blue Book: China Minor Internet Usage Report indicates that watching videos has surpassed playing games and listening to music, ranking first among internet activities for minors, accounting for 47.5%. The proportion of minors using short video apps like Kwai and TikTok is as high as 65.3%, making short videos an essential platform for their online life. Statistics show that the usage of short video apps among elementary school students has reached 66%, even higher than that of high school students (62.7%) [ 7 ]. Prior research has explored chiefly the psychological mechanisms through which media usage negatively affects academic performance from the perspectives of internet addiction or social media usage [ 11 – 13 ]. Some scholars have examined the appeal of social media to minors from the perspective of attachment, suggesting that minors form emotional connections and care when interacting with online communities [ 3 , 14 ]. In comparison to the extensive research on the effects of "addiction" and "attachment" on minors, further research is needed to deepen the understanding of how specific media like short videos may influence minors. Additionally, the underlying conditions of psychological activities before the influence of short video usage on academic performance need to be further explored. Excessive media usage may lead to various learning issues, such as attention deficits, poor time management, and reduced study time [ 3 ]. Given that short videos are rich in visual and auditory elements and can convey a vast amount of information in a short time frame. The study explores how short videos might affect minors’ "attention," which is a constant psychological process, spans, and academic performance, based on the Attention Restoration Theory(ART). It suggests that the appealing content of such videos could lead to attention deficits, poor time management, and less study time, impacting their academic results. The Ecological Systems Theory from Bronfenbrenner [ 15 ] posits that the family is one of the most direct and micro-level systems influencing individual development. As a "microsystem," the family plays a pivotal role in the growth and development of children, making it a crucial component of factors sensitive to social differences [ 16 ]. Chinese parents typically have high expectations for their children’s academic success and tend to control or regulate their media usage [ 17 ]. However, compared to restrictive control and intervention, parents’ actions and attitudes at home may profoundly influence their children [ 18 ]. For example, parents’ media behaviors and attitudes toward their children’s media usage can significantly shape their values and behavioral guidelines [ 19 ]. Likewise, parents’ usage duration of short videos at home may subtly affect their children’s media usage habits and time allocation [ 9 ]. The study aims to investigate whether the attentional processes influenced by the use of short videos could be a significant internal factor contributing to the negative impact on academic performance among minors.

extractedSections.heading: 2.1 Short video usage and academic performance
extractedSections.text: Children are exposed to various forms of screen time and electronic device usage in today’s digital age. Research indicates that the use of electronic devices is negatively correlated with academic performance, regardless of gender, age, or family background [ 20 ]. A systematic review and meta-analysis covering 480,479 samples revealed a negative correlation between children and adolescents’ television viewing, video game playing, and academic performance. As the time spent by children and adolescents watching TV and playing video games increases, their overall grades, language scores, and math scores tend to decrease [ 20 ]. Likewise, studies indicate that excessive use of short videos can impact students’ engagement negatively behaviorally but positively emotionally and cognitively [ 21 , 22 ]. Elementary school students are in the third stage, the "Concrete Operational Stage," according to Piaget’s Cognitive Development Theory. In this stage, children can engage in logical thinking and operations, but these are based on specific objects and events they observe and interact with [ 23 ]. The time displacement hypothesis suggests that spending more time on television and electronic games reduces the time children spend on other activities beneficial for cognitive development, such as physical exercise, verbal communication, studying, or sleep. This reduction in cognitive effort may impact academic performance [ 10 ]. This aligns with the findings of previous studies that excessive screen time, including mobile device usage, might lead to poorer academic performance in children [ 24 ]. This explanation corresponds to the perspective that excessive screen time, including the use of short videos, can negatively impact academic performance. Short videos are often designed with highly appealing visuals and fast-paced, engaging content, which may lead to addiction among young users [ 25 ]. This addictive nature can result in prolonged engagement, potentially diverting students’ time and energy from studying. As students spend more time watching short videos, the time available for completing assignments and studying might decrease [ 26 ]. The Cognitive Load Theory suggests that learning can be hindered when individuals are simultaneously presented with excessive information [ 27 ]. Videos often convey information rapidly, demanding viewers to process a large amount of content within a short period. For elementary school students whose cognitive abilities are still developing, excessive exposure to such stimulating content may lead to an overload of cognitive load, subsequently impairing academic performance [ 28 ]. Some scholars explain the relationship between short video usage and academic performance from the perspective of media multitasking. Media multitasking refers to engaging in multiple media activities simultaneously, such as watching short videos while sending comments or socializing [ 29 ]. Individuals frequently involved in media multitasking may exhibit lower cognitive control and reduced attentional abilities [ 30 ]. This implies that users of short videos, especially elementary school students, might experience compromised cognitive control if they frequently switch between learning tasks and watching short videos, affecting their academic performance. Furthermore, the potential impact of short video usage on academic performance might be influenced by the type of content consumed. Although some short videos have educational value, underage individuals cannot judge the value of the content provided in short videos. Most short videos primarily focus on pure entertainment, which can disrupt underage individuals’ mental faculties [ 9 , 31 – 33 ]. In conclusion, this paper proposes a hypothesis.

extractedSections.heading: 2.2 Short video usage, attention, and academic performance
extractedSections.text: The Attention Restoration Theory (ART) proposed by Kaplan and Kaplan [ 34 ] suggests that natural environments can restore cognitive functions, including attention, which might be depleted after prolonged focused attention (such as focusing on screens). While ART primarily relates to the therapeutic benefits of natural environments, it provides an insightful conceptual framework for extrapolating this theory to the context of short video usage. Since natural environments can restore attention, excessive use of short videos, with their captivating features, essentially depletes students’ attentional resources, continuously diverting their focus to screen content. Previous research has provided direct evidence linking screen media use to increased attention issues in childhood, such as children spending more than two hours daily watching TV or playing screen games more likely to have concentration problems [ 33 ]. The use of digital entertainment products has been positively correlated with Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) [ 35 ]. Additionally, Lang’s Limited Capacity Model of Motivated Mediated Message Processing (LC4MP) [ 36 ] indirectly provides clues for understanding the potential risks of short video usage on students’ attention to academic tasks. This model posits that individuals have limited cognitive capacity for processing information, influenced by media content characteristics and individual motivation. In short video usage, the LC4MP model can be understood as short videos being designed to be highly attractive and engaging, diverting students’ attention excessively towards watching the videos and subsequently neglecting academic tasks, thus scattering their attention. The model further suggests that when media content triggers viewers’ motivation, they invest more cognitive resources, potentially causing more significant interference with students’ academic tasks. Therefore, the allure of short videos and students’ usage behavior might be critical factors affecting their concentration. Attention difficulties impact the academic performance of children and adolescents, which is a significant concern in education and psychology. As an illustration, ADHD patients typically struggle to maintain focus for extended periods and are easily distracted by external stimuli, severely affecting their academic achievements [ 37 ]. Attention difficulties might lead to students struggling to maintain focus, being easily distracted, and consequently spending more time and effort on tasks. This group of students must invest more time and energy than their peers to complete academic tasks, adversely affecting their academic performance [ 38 ]. Yang and Chen’s study [ 39 ] indicated that students with ADHD often exhibit lower academic scores and poorer learning skills, as they cannot fully engage in classroom activities and easily miss essential teaching content, resulting in comparatively lower levels of knowledge and understanding. This affects their exam scores and can lead to higher dropout rates. Moreover, Short video addiction is linked to avoiding learning and lacking commitment, while study avoidance is associated with silent classroom behavior. Parents and educators should be aware of the negative impact of short video addiction on learning behavior [ 21 ]. The proliferation of short video usage poses new challenges to the attention of children and adolescents. The diverse and ever-changing visual and auditory stimuli on short video platforms constantly pull individuals’ attention. Anderson and Dill [ 40 ] highlighted the attentional drain caused by electronic media, where fast-paced stimuli and sustained interactivity in electronic games can lead to players’ attention being scattered, making it difficult to focus on other tasks for extended periods. This situation also likely exists in short videos since they often possess similar stimulating properties. From the perspective of multitasking, Guo and Liu’s study [ 41 ] found that content on electronic devices usually requires more frequent attention switches than traditional media. This frequent switching might train users to shift their attention rapidly among multiple information sources. Still, it could also decrease the ability to sustain singular-task attention for prolonged periods. This is challenging for learning tasks since students typically need to concentrate on a single subject or task for extended periods. Students who excessively use electronic devices are more prone to attention problems. Moreover, over time, these students become increasingly reliant on short videos, making it more challenging to focus on tasks requiring concentrated attention [ 42 ]. Thus, short video usage might adversely affect individuals’ attention, and those who frequently use electronic media tend to perform poorly on tasks requiring focused attention in their daily lives [ 21 , 43 ]. In summary, existing studies provide preliminary evidence supporting the relationship between short video usage, attention, and academic performance.

extractedSections.heading: 2.3 Parental short video usage duration as a moderator from a family environment perspective
extractedSections.text: According to the Social Cognitive Theory, environmental and cognitive factors often influence a child’s behavior [ 44 ]. Nie, Zheng, and Zhang [ 45 ] emphasized the importance of the family environment, encompassing both physical aspects (such as home arrangement and atmosphere) and psychological factors (such as family rules and cultural values), in a child’s growth. Research has demonstrated the significant impact of the family environment on a child’s media usage behavior [ 46 ]. Parental media usage behavior may influence a child’s media habits and attention through its impact on the family environment. Specifically, when parents frequently use short-form videos, children might imitate their behavior and develop similar usage patterns [ 44 ]. Moreover, parents’ attitudes toward media usage may subtly shape children’s media behavior. Suppose children frequently observe their parents using short-form video apps at home. In that case, they may perceive it as a standard and acceptable behavior, leading to its normalization within the family values [ 47 ]. In a family-oriented context, parental behaviors and attitudes will demonstrate a modeling effect on a child’s behavior [ 48 , 49 ]. Researchers like Jordan et al. [ 50 ] and Hefner et al. [ 51 ] have shown that parents’ own media consumption significantly influences children’s media usage duration, highlighting the impactful modeling effect of parental media behavior. Parental media usage patterns might negatively impact a child’s attention. When parents frequently engage with social media applications, their attention might be diverted, affecting their ability to concentrate during interactions with their children. This diversion could indirectly lead to the child’s reduced attention during parent-child interactions [ 52 , 53 ]. Parents may use mobile media as an entertainment tool during quality time with their children, reducing interactive opportunities and missing chances to enhance the child’s attention levels [ 47 ]. Therefore, this study incorporates parental short video usage duration to investigate and refine the influence and mechanisms between elementary school students’ short video usage and attention.

extractedSections.heading: 2.4 Research hypothesis
extractedSections.text: H1 : The higher the level of short video usage among elementary school students , the lower their academic performance . H2 : The higher the level of short video usage among elementary school students , the weaker their attention . H3 : Attention plays a mediating role in the relationship between short video usage and academic performance . H4 : Parental short video usage duration positively moderates the relationship between elementary school students’ short video usage and attention , exacerbating the negative impact of students’ short video usage on their attention and further affecting their academic performance . acceptedSources.title: Adolescent user behaviors on short video application, cognitive functioning and academic performance
acceptedSources.abstract: Despite the soaring popularity of short video applications (SVA) among adolescents worldwide, little is known about its potential impact on adolescent users. This study aimed to examine whether and how adolescents’ user behaviors regarding SVA, including daily usage and reliance on algorithmic recommendations, predict their cognitive functioning and academic performance. A sample of Chinese adolescents from two age cohorts (Mage=12.25, SD=0.02, N=454; Mage=15.21, SD=0.02, N= 368) completed the survey on SVA user behavior and cognitive ability test regarding academic delay of gratification (ADOG), working memory and verbal ability. The findings reveal that daily usage of SVA is negatively correlated with users’ ADOG and academic performance for both age cohorts. And the dependency on algorithmic personalization negatively predicts the working memory, verbal ability and academic performance of the younger cohort only. Also, their SVA daily usage negatively correlates with working memory and verbal ability, which both simultaneously mediate between their user behavior and poorer academic performance. Considering the age differences in SVA-related effects, the study further points out the higher susceptibility of younger adolescents to SVA use compared to their older counterparts, which should be noted by students, parents, educators and researchers to prevent the potentially negative impact.

evidencePoints: Despite the soaring popularity of short video applications (SVA) among adolescents worldwide, little is known about its potential impact on adolescent users. This study aimed to examine whether and how adolescents’ user behaviors regarding SVA, including daily usage and reliance on algorithmic recommendations, predict their cognitive functioning and academic performance. A sample of Chinese adolescents from two age cohorts (Mage=12.25, SD=0.02, N=454; Mage=15.21, SD=0.02, N= 368) completed the survey on SVA user behavior and cognitive ability test regarding academic delay of gratification (ADOG), working memory and verbal ability. The findings reveal that daily usage of SVA is negatively correlated with users’ ADOG and academic performance for both age cohorts. And the dependency on algorithmic personalization negatively predicts the working memory, verbal ability and academic performance of the younger cohort only. Also, their SVA daily usage negatively correlates with working memory and verbal ability, which both simultaneously mediate between their user behavior and poorer academic performance. Considering the age differences in SVA-related effects, the study further points out the higher susceptibility of younger adolescents to SVA use compared to their older counterparts, which should be noted by students, parents, educators and researchers to prevent the potentially negative impact.

acceptedSources.title: The Influence of Short-Duration Video Content on Short-Term Memory in Junior High School Students
acceptedSources.abstract: The increasing consumption of short-form video content, such as TikTok, Instagram Reels, and YouTube Shorts, has raised concerns regarding its impact on cognitive functions, particularly short-term memory. This study aimed to examine the effect of short duration video exposure on short-term memory performance among students at Yayasan Irtiqo Kebajikan. An experimental method with a two-group design was employed, consisting of an experimental group that watched short duration videos for 180 seconds and a control group that received no video exposure prior to the memory test. The participants were 40 students selected through random sampling. Short-term memory was measured using the ME Test, a subtest of the Intelligenz Struktur Test (IST), which assesses the ability to recall a series of words. The results of statistical analysis indicated a significant difference between the experimental and control groups (p < 0.05), with the experimental group demonstrating lower short-term memory scores. These findings suggest that exposure to short-form video content may negatively affect individuals ability to store and process information in short-term memory, highlighting the importance of managing digital media consumption among children and adolescents.

acceptedSources.abstract: The short-form video has emerged as one of the most popular social media content among Gen Z and millennials. Generally, video content that does not exceed 3 minutes is considered short-form. acceptedSources.title: Hubungan antara Short-Form Video Adiction dengan Kualitas Tidur Remaja
acceptedSources.abstract: Latar Belakang: Kecanduan video pendek pada remaja telah menjadi fenomena yang semakin berkembang dengan adanya platform media sosial yang menyajikan video berdurasi singkat, seperti TikTok dan Instagram reels. Penggunaan yang berlebihan terhadap konten ini telah dikaitkan dengan gangguan kualitas tidur remaja. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengetahui hubungan antara kecanduan video pendek dengan kualitas tidur remaja di SMAN 3 Sumedang. Metode: Metode kuantitatif korelasional dengan pendekatan cross-sectional. Sampel penelitian terdiri dari 304 responden yang dipilih secara acak proporsional. Data dikumpulkan menggunakan kuesioner Short Video Addiction Scale (SVAS) untuk mengukur kecanduan video pendek dan Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) untuk menilai kualitas tidur. Hasil: Analisis menunjukkan adanya hubungan yang signifikan antara kecanduan video pendek dengan kualitas tidur (p-value 0.001), dimana semakin tinggi tingkat kecanduan terhadap video pendek, semakin buruk kualitas tidur yang dialami oleh remaja. Kesimpulan dari penelitian ini adalah bahwa kecanduan video pendek berperan dalam menurunnya kualitas tidur remaja, yang dapat berpengaruh pada kesehatan fisik dan mental mereka. Disarankan agar remaja diberikan edukasi mengenai dampak negatif penggunaan video pendek pada kualitas tidur mereka dan pengelolaan penggunaan media digital secara bijak.

acceptedSources.title: Attentional impulsivity, short-form video use and adolescents’ school misbehaviors: mediating role of parental media mediation
acceptedSources.abstract: Short-form video use (SVU) is getting increasingly popular among adolescents. However, its associations with adolescents’ school misbehaviors have been largely overlooked in previous literature. Drawing on the parental mediation theory, the current study examined the associations of SVU and attentional impulsivity with adolescents’ school misbehaviors, as well as the mediating role of parental mediation. Using a cross-sectional design, a sample of Chinese adolescents (N = 839) was employed. The proposed relationships were examined using Structural Equation Modeling (SEM). The results revealed that attentional impulsivity was positively associated with SVU. Both attentional impulsivity and SVU were positively related to school misbehavior, controlling for covariates. Moreover, active parental media mediation strategies were found to mediate the relationship between attentional impulsivity and school misbehavior. These findings highlight SVU as a negative correlate of school performance, particularly in relation to impulsivity. Potential interventions are recommended to focus on active parental media mediation strategies, such as engaging in open discussions with children. Interventions targeting adolescents’ self-esteem or related factors should also be considered.
